title: Phase 8 cache-off measurements before and after zero-interval concurrency fix

conditions.declared_slo: p95 <= 30s, >= 1 completed run/s, zero failed runs with 3 workers

root_cause.before: OpenAICompat.chat held one per-process lock during every HTTP request, even when min_interval_s was zero. Four worker threads therefore serialized their LLM requests and occupied slots while waiting.
root_cause.after: The lock and interval wait are used only when min_interval_s is positive. At zero, concurrent requests proceed without provider interval throttling. Positive configured intervals remain serialized and spaced.

old_cache_off.historical_queue_run_call_split: unavailable: the original isolated Redis volumes were removed; saved Locust CSVs contain end-to-end timings only

slo_result.one_worker_comparison: p95 and throughput fail the numeric targets; the first rolling p95 breach is at 24 users

data_notes: Run and call means are computed from completed uncached Redis run records and their traces.
The 3-worker API counter showed 601 runs while this aggregation found 600 completed uncached run records and Locust recorded 600 submissions/599 E2E rows; the discrepancy is unresolved.
The 1-worker Locust E2E count is one below submissions; all 295 submitted runs were present as completed uncached records after the queue drained.
